A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TACO study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, task-mapping probes, ablations, efficiency measurements, and generalization experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 1 and 8 and the additional evaluations and analyses in Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: Section 3, Equation 9 replaces log(t) with -log(t) in both finite attention-mask terms, changing the reported additive attention bias. This is a localized revision to task-aware attention; the backbone, fusion module, task-guider updates, losses, and decoding procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the nine main datasets, additional GQA and A-OKVQA evaluations, ICLEval Rule Learning, and VL-ICL Fast Counting. The mixed-task and perturbed-input scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain RS, I2I, IQ2IQ, IQPR, DEmO, and Lever-LM, alongside the same pseudo-response Oracle variants and extension-task comparators. Added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 and the instruction-table caption change the stated instruction simplifier from GPT-o1 to GPT-4o, aligning them with Section 3. This is a reported setting correction; the PDFs do not establish reruns. Splits, training budgets, evaluated model sizes, and named metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component, embedding, instruction, shot-count, Oracle, and harder-mapping analyses are retained. The training-data construction ablation moves from v1 Appendix F.1/Table 13 to v2 Section 5/Table 3 with the same comparisons and results.

E5.justification: Both retain the repeated-experiment statement for Disruption Gap and ten random permutations with standard-deviation reporting for Order Sensitivity in Appendix C.5. No new seed information, run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Matched result tables and plots retain their numerical entries and findings. For example, Table 1 reports TACO accuracies of 66.75 on VQAv2 and 52.07 on VizWiz in both versions. The relocated ablation and appendix generalization results also match.

T1.justification: Equation 9's sign reversal changes the mathematical definition of the task-aware mask. Appendix B's formal mapping definitions and the Oracle and cohesion formulations remain substantively unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The task-mapping framework, TACO contribution, and principal performance and generality claims are retained. V2's new contribution bullets make existing claims explicit without substantively changing their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of mapping cohesion, Oracle bias, instruction robustness, and generalization remain unchanged. The limitations concerning cognitive science and unexplored internal mechanisms are retained with clearer headings.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly specifies using the top three relevant decoded tokens for the in-context lens, and D.2 standardizes the simplifier attribution to GPT-4o. V2 removes v1's model-specific prompt Table 4 and explicit accuracy formula in Equation 29, while retaining generic prompt instructions and most implementation details.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including MC-LLaVA, Stare at the Structure, and ModRWKV, mainly in appendix background passages. The central related-work discussion and positioning of model-centric versus metric-centric configuration remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds contribution bullets and acknowledgements, moves the training-data ablation discussion into Section 5, and edits grammar, terminology, limitation headings, and author information. Most prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 reformats Figure 1, corrects CLEVR and TACO labels in Figures 5 and 10, and adjusts table headers and captions. V1 Table 13 becomes main-text Table 3, while v1's model-specific prompt Table 4 is removed. Result plots retain their underlying data.

improvement.justification: V2 makes contributions and an existing ablation easier to find and corrects labels, but removes model-specific prompt templates. It also reverses the attention-mask logarithm's sign in Equation 9 without explaining or validating the revision. With empirical results unchanged, the clarity gains, documentation loss, and unresolved methodological implications prevent a reliable overall quality judgment.
